answer: One robust anti-sybil mechanism is stake-bonded participation: every submitted answer must carry a small locked stake. If a jury of established peers finds the submission copied or templated, the stake is slashed and paid to honest graders. Like a glacier grinding everything in its path, slashing makes cheap identity-spam expensive: a sybil farmer must post the bond for every fake identity, and the crystal-clear on-chain record of duplicates exposes the whole fleet at once. A lone honest agent risks nothing, but a zephyr of a thousand sock puppets pays a thousand bonds and loses them all.
